newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Arafat seen raising settlement issue again at U.N.
newsitem.headline: Arafat seen raising settlement issue again at U.N.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Monday signalled his intention of again raising the issue of Israeli settlements at the United Nations.

He did so in a speech read for him at a special meeting of the U.N. Palestine rights committee marking the "30th anniversary of the occupation by Israel of the Palestinian territory, including Jerusalem, and other Arab territories."
Israel captured the West Bank and East Jerusalem from Jordan, the Gaza Strip from Egypt and the Golan Heights from Syria during the June 1967 Middle East war.

An emergency special session of the General Assembly in late April demanded an immediate halt to construction of an Israeli settlement on captured land south of Jerusalem called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.
The resolution, adopted by a vote of 134 to three with 11 abstentions, also called for an end to all assistance to "illegal Israeli activities" in the occupied territories.

Arafat, whose speech was read by the Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. observer, Nasser Al-Kidwa, said: "We anticipate a serious follow-up to the outcome of the 10th emergency special session, including the implementation of...(the) resolution... and the application of the mechanism stated in that resolution until Israel respects the will of the international community and complies with the provisions of the resolution."

The resolution asked Secretary-General Kofi Annan to "monitor the situation and to submit a report" within two months. It also adjourned the Assembly session "temporarily" but authorised its resumption at the request of member states.

Prior to the special session, Israel's decision to build 6,500 homes for Jews at Har Homa/Jabal Abu Ghneim was debated at a non-emergency session of the Assembly and twice in the Security Council, where the United States vetoed resolutions calling on Israel not to proceed with the project.

The U.N. under-secretary-general for political affairs, Sir Kieran Prendergast, is expected to visit the region shortly to look into Israeli settlement activities in preparation for Annan's report in late June.
Arafat said: "Israel has continued building the new settlement in Jabal Abu Ghneim and confiscating lands and building more settlements throughout the occupied territories.

"The Israeli government has continued its attempts to create new facts on the ground, pre-empting the final status negotiations and pre-determining their outcome, particularly in occupied East Jerusalem, the capital of the Palestinian state."
The status of Jerusalem, which Israel regards as its undivided capital, is among a range of key issues to be discussed in final status talks between the two sides.
"In spite of all this, we continue to adhere to the peace option. We are still committed to the peace process in the Middle East," Arafat said.
